Governors
Nationally school governors are the largest volunteer force in the country. Governors at Shottermill Junior School are people from all walks of life who bring enthusiasm, commitment and an interest in education to this important role. We believe that the school should provide a safe and supportive environment where each child is able to flourish - it is the Governors' responsibility to ensure that the school achieves this aim.
Governors meet throughout the year as a Full Governing Body with two meetings each term - designed to focus on either Resources or Children and Learning. Most Governors also have an area of special responsibility, such as: Safeguarding, SEND, Pupil Premium or Wellbeing. Each Governor is also assigned one of our School Development Key Priorities to oversee throughout the year. More information about the persons elected to our Governing Body is available on the Committee Membership and Attendance page.
If you are interested in becoming a Governor at our school, or you would like to make contact with one of our Governors, please do so by contacting the School Office who will be able to put you in touch with the Co Chair of Governors - Mrs Beth Niven and Mr Christopher Bongard

Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Shottermill Junior School where our children benefit from an engaging and creative approach to learning, which aims to foster children’s enthusiasm and commitment to succeed in all aspects of school life.
Our high quality environment ensures children’s learning is exceptional. All children have an equal opportunity to thrive across all areas of the curriculum and are very well supported academically as well as personally in our safe and disciplined school.
Shottermill is a truly unique and special place and we pride ourselves on our effective partnerships with parents, guardians and the wider community. We look forward to welcoming you along to meet us in the near future, where you will quickly find that together we share the same goal - to ensure that every child receives the very best education possible at our school.
Mrs Kate Barnes Headteacher

Music
At Shottermill Junior School, we are passionate about Music and we have been awarded the Music Mark. We fully agree with the following statement taken from: The power of music to change lives A National Plan for Music Education - June 2022.
'Music is a cornerstone of the broad and balanced education that every child should receive. It touches hearts and minds, it celebrates and challenges, and it connects us and moves us.'
At our school we provide an hour of Music to every child, in every year group, each week. This is delivered through our dedicated Specialist Music Teacher, which we feel sets us apart from many other Primary settings, where Music is usually delivered by a Class Teacher.
Music lessons are taught in our Dance Studio, but additional space is provided for small group tuition in our Music Practice Room. We teach whole school singing in the Main Hall, which has a newly installed sound system and stage lighting for hosting summer productions and special assemblies.
We provide peripatetic Music lessons throughout the week:
Surrey Arts - further information can be found by following this link.
SAM Music Service provides 20-30 minute 1:1 music lessons, allowing your child the opportunity of learning to play the guitar, drum kit, piano/keyboard or to sing. To enquire, complete the short contact form on SAM’s website (www.sammusicservice.com), and they’ll be in touch soon, or you can email lessons@sammusicservice.com, or call 01273 465122 to speak to one of their friendly team. The team will also offer a free taster session to any interested families.

Special Educational Needs Provision
Provision for pupils with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities
At Shottermill Junior School we are committed to ensuring that all children are well supported and we pride ourselves on our fully inclusive approach to teaching and learning. We work extremely hard to ensure that all children have equal access to the same educational experiences and the broad and balanced curriculum on offer at our school, which aims to foster children’s curiosity and develop their independence and love of learning.
We are committed to working with parents and outside agencies to ensure that pupils who require additional support, are identified early on and the appropriate provision is put in place. We operate on the cycle of: Assess, Plan, Do, Review, whilst fully involving children and parents in the process.
From September 2014, the Government published new information on how schools should ensure children with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) should be identified and supported in their learning.
The links below provide further information for parents on these SEND reforms, Surrey’s approach and clarifies the Wave 1, 2 and 3 provision that is currently available at our school. There is also information on our Local Offer and our new SEND Policy.
If you require any further information or are concerned about your child’s development, please get in touch with our Special Education Needs Coordinator (SENCo) Mrs Zoe Jones, by emailing: senco@shottermill-jun.surrey.sch.uk
We are committed to ensuring that we are an inclusive school which caters for all differing abilities and needs. If however you are a parent and wish to raise a concern about your child's provision at our school, please follow the process outlined in the Complaints Principles & Procedures document which can be located here.

Absence
Good attendance and punctuality at school is essential and any days away from school interrupt teaching and learning and hinders the progress that children make. Repeatedly arriving late at school is also very disruptive and we would like to remind parents that our gates open at 8:35am and we want our children to arrive at this time, as many of our catch-up interventions run first thing in the morning. Registration is 8:50am every day. We realise that from time to time, children are unwell so please ensure you inform the School Office before 9am if your child will be away from school for illness and please continue to update us daily if your child remains unable to attend school.
Holiday taken during term time will not be authorised, which reflects DfE statutory guidance published August 2024. We would like to also draw your attention to recent changes in the issuing of Penalty Notices, for non-attendance at school, as set out in our policy below (which has been developed in partnership with Shottermill Infant School).
In all instances, parents or guardians must request in advance permission from the Headteacher to take their child out of school during term time (please use the form provided below). It is especially important that at key points during the academic year children attend school, for example during National Curriculum Tests in Year 6 or during the end of the summer term/beginning of the autumn term, when all important transition takes place.
Our Home School Link Worker - Katherine Bourne is also able to offer support with attendance issues, as is Mrs Barnes, the Senior Attendance Champion. If you would like to make an appointment to discuss your child's attendance, please do so via the School Office. If after providing support and early help, we notice that attendance remains a concern, we may refer families to the Surrey Attendance Service.

School Clubs
Each term we are pleased to be able to offer a variety of clubs for children to participate in and which run either before, during or after school. Some clubs are provided by members of staff in school and some may be organised by external providers, for which there may be a charge.
They may include French, Choir, Gardening, Computing and various sports clubs, to name but a few. After school clubs usually run from 3:10pm – 4:15pm unless there are special timings which we or the club provider will let you know about.
In addition to our usual after school clubs, the school also hosts Koosa Kids - an external childcare provider. Please click here for more information.
At the beginning of each term you will receive a letter showing the clubs on offer for the term ahead, as well as the dates that the clubs will commence and finish. In most cases, clubs do not run during the week of Parent Consultation Evening.
Please complete one form to request your child’s place at the clubs of their choice and return this to the Class Teacher/School Office (you may need to complete separate forms for externally run clubs – providing payment directly to them). A slip is sent out confirming your child’s place at the club(s) chosen at the start of each term.
We expect children to be committed to attending their clubs each week but if your child is unable to attend, please inform the School Office to ensure all children are accounted for.

Handwriting Expectations
Handwriting is an essential skill that supports the transcription and spelling element of the National Curriculum for English. Children are required to consistently use joined handwriting in order to achieve the expected standard by the end of Year 6.
In order to develop a consistent approach across both Shottermill Infant and Junior Schools, we have adopted a shared Shottermill Handwriting Code, which is shown below. This approach embraces the mantra 'start on the line and you'll be fine' as a fun way to remember the correct formation of each letter.
Below are some expectations of the quality of handwriting we expect by the end of each year group, which we hope will guide parents in supporting good cursive writing when working on homework tasks. We regularly teach handwriting lessons in class, often incorporating the weekly spellings children are learning in the week. Children also publish their extended writing usually every 2 weeks, as part of our English lessons.
Expectation by the end of Year 3: Below is an example which shows the standard of handwriting expected by the end of Year 3. Here the letters are mostly formed correctly with ascenders and descenders of suitable size. Capital letters stand out from lower case letters because they are correctly formed. Most letters are correctly joined, but this is still developing.
Expectation by the end of Year 4: Below is an example which shows the standard of handwriting expected by the end of Year 4. All letter joins are correctly formed, with accurate ascenders and descenders. The size of handwriting is more suitable and consistent.
Expectation by the end of Year 5: Below is an example which shows the standard of handwriting expected by the end of Year 5. Writing is consistently well joined and cursive, with a personal style starting to develop. The size of letter formation is consistent and the child's handwriting is able to be maintained over longer pieces of writing.
Expectation by the end of Year 6: We would expect children to be competently able to join their handwriting, showing a high level of consistency, particularly throughout the entire piece of work and when writing at speed.
